office_does: A Benton County District Court judge, elected countywide for four years, hears misdemeanor and gross-misdemeanor cases, traffic and other infractions, small claims, anti-harassment matters and civil cases up to $100,000. The main discretion is in release, sentencing, probation and therapeutic-court supervision.
race_blurb: Open seat: Judge Terry Tanner is not on the ballot. Longtime Tri-Cities contract prosecutor Mike Rio, endorsed by Tanner, the rest of the District Court bench, local prosecutors and police groups, faces attorney and King County pro tem judge Talesha Sams. Sams's career mixes prosecution, public defense and Adult Protective Services work, and she lost to Tanner for this seat in 2018.

candidates.summary: Benton City attorney with 25 years of practice as a prosecutor, public defender, private practitioner and DSHS Adult Protective Services attorney; King County District Court judge pro tem since 2015 and an Army veteran.
highlights: King County District Court judge pro tem since 2015 [S1][S2]
Former Adams County deputy prosecutor; has also worked as a public defender [S1][S2]
Says she "would uphold the law and would not legislate any personal agenda" [S1]
Lost the 2018 race for this seat to Judge Tanner, 34.5% to 65.5% [S3]

safety.basis: Mixed formation: prosecutor in District and Superior Court, public defender, private practice, Adult Protective Services attorney and Veterans Court mentor; no bail or diversion position.

experience.basis: Not an incumbent, but runs on 25 years of varied practice and more than ten years as a District Court pro tem judge.

candidates.summary: Tri-Cities contract city and district-court prosecutor since 2005 (Spokane County deputy prosecutor from 2002), Franklin County District Court judge pro tem and Benton City hearing examiner; campaigns on consistency and accountability.
highlights: 21 years prosecuting district-court cases for Tri-Cities-area cities and counties [S1][S3]
Franklin County District Court judge pro tem; Benton City hearing examiner since 2007 [S1][S3]
Endorsed by incumbent Tanner, all Benton-Franklin Superior Court judges, local prosecutors and police groups [S4]

safety.basis: Career formed almost entirely in prosecution, plus law-enforcement training; campaigns on accountability and lower recidivism with prosecutor and police endorsements; no bail or diversion position.

experience.basis: Not an incumbent, but runs on two decades of district-court prosecution and pro tem service, endorsed by the Position 1 incumbent and most local judges.
